newsitem.title: GERMANY: Paper says IMF believes Germany will meet EMU goal.
newsitem.headline: Paper says IMF believes Germany will meet EMU goal.

text.p: A German newspaper reported on Tuesday that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) believes Germany will meet the budget deficit criterion for Europe's planned single currency.

The Berliner Zeitung, citing IMF experts, said the 1997 budget deficit would initially be 3.1 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), but "statistical refinements" would revise the figure down so Germany could post a figure of three percent.

A finance ministry spokesman, contacted at home about the report released on Tuesday evening ahead of publication on Wednesday, said he could not confirm the IMF figure but added, "We welcome any predictions which confirm our own assumptions."

The Maastricht Treaty lays down a figure of three percent of GDP. Fierce debate has surrounded how loosely this can be interpreted, but Chancellor Helmut Kohl has pledged Germany will meet 3.0 percent -- the strictest version of the target.

The ministry spokesman confirmed another part of the newspaper's report, which said Germany would receive a boost in its bid to meet the currency criteria by taking hosptial debts out of public accounts, as other European countries do.

"This is nothing new," the spokesman said, adding the move was part of a drive by Eurostat, the European statistics office, to standardise acounting practises in the run-up to economic and monetary union (EMU).
"This is not creative accounting," he added. "We have been asked to undertake this measure."
The Berliner Zeitung said taking the hospital debt out of the public accounts would make a difference of 0.2 percentage points to the deficit.

The spokesman confirmed the change would have an influence on the economic data for 1997 -- the basis for selecting EMU candidates -- but he could not say offhand if this would be more likely to affect the deficit or debt criteria.
The Berliner Zeitung said the finance ministry would issue a new deficit forecast of three percent of GDP on September 1.
The spokesman said he knew of no plans to make such a forecast, adding that Germany had already made clear it expected to meet the deficit target.
